quitSmoking.title: Quit Smoking Calculator
quitSmoking.subtitle: From your quit date and daily habit, see how long you've been smoke-free, the money saved, cigarettes not smoked and the health recovery timeline. Korea's free quit-smoking support programs are summarized too.

input.title: Your smoking habit
input.startDefault: No quit date yet, so this shows an example of quitting 30 days ago. Change the date and it's saved on this device.
input.startHint: Your inputs are saved only on this device (browser).
input.dailyHint: The default of 10 is just an example. Enter how many you usually smoke.

priceHint.cig: Default ₩4,500: typical Korean cigarette price since 2015 (Newsis, Mar 2026)
priceHint.heat: Default ₩4,800: IQOS TEREA suggested retail price (Insight, Aug 2026)

input.monthlyHint: The default of ₩100,000 is an example. There's no official figure, so enter what you actually spent.
input.err: Enter a whole number from {min} to {max}

result.label: Smoke-free for
result.future: Your quit time hasn't come yet ({v} from now). Counting starts then.
result.lifeNote: About 20 minutes per cigarette, average for British smokers (UCL, Addiction 2024). Varies widely by person.
result.keepNote: Total from your quit date at today's prices. Price rises would make it bigger.
result.savings: What if you saved {v} a month? Open the savings calculator

next.title: Next recovery milestone
next.allDone: You've passed every WHO milestone, up to 15 years

withdrawal.peak: Withdrawal is usually strongest in the first 2–3 days and eases within 2–4 weeks (MSD Manual).
withdrawal.easing: The hardest 2–3 days are behind you. Withdrawal usually eases within 2–4 weeks (MSD Manual).

record.title: Your record
record.none: No longest streak saved yet. If you smoke again, tap 'Restart' and your streak so far is kept as a record.
record.confirmDesc: Your current streak ({v}) is compared with your longest streak and kept, and your quit time is reset to now.
record.local: Your record stays on this device (browser) and is never sent to a server.
record.storageError: Browser storage is unavailable (private mode, etc.), so your record can't be saved.

timeline.title: How your body recovers
timeline.desc: Recovery milestones after quitting, from the WHO. Past milestones are marked done; upcoming ones show the time left.
timeline.ecig: These milestones come from people who quit cigarettes. They may not apply directly if you only used e-cigarettes.
timeline.src: Source: WHO, 'Tobacco: health benefits of smoking cessation' (2020-02-25). A month counts as 30 days and a year as 365 days.

min20.text: Your heart rate and blood pressure drop.

h12.text: The carbon monoxide level in your blood drops to normal.

w2to12.text: Your circulation improves and your lung function increases.

m1to9.text: Coughing and shortness of breath decrease.

y1.text: Your risk of coronary heart disease is about half that of a smoker.

y5.text: Your stroke risk falls to that of a non-smoker 5 to 15 years after quitting.

y10.text: Your lung cancer risk falls to about half that of a smoker, and the risk of mouth, throat, esophagus, bladder, cervix and pancreas cancer decreases.

y15.text: Your risk of coronary heart disease is that of a non-smoker.

support.title: Free quit-smoking support in Korea
support.desc: Checked on each agency's website on 2026-11-22. Details vary by region and provider, so confirm before you sign up.

clinic.title: Public health center cessation clinic
points: Local public health centers run a 6-month quit-smoking program.
One-on-one counseling, plus free nicotine patches, gum and other aids when needed (Seoul guidance).
Find and book a nearby center on the No Smoke Guide website.
clinic.link: Find one on No Smoke Guide

nhis.title: Clinic and hospital treatment (National Health Insurance)
points: Up to 6 visits with counseling and prescriptions over 8–12 weeks at a participating clinic, up to 3 rounds a year.
You pay 20% for visits 1–2 and nothing for visits 3–6. Medical aid recipients and the bottom 20% by premium pay nothing for visits and cessation drugs.
Complete the program (6 visits, or the drug course: bupropion 56+ days, varenicline or nicotine aids 84 days) and your visit 1–2 copayments are refunded.

call.title: Quitline 1544-9030
points: One-on-one phone counseling tailored to your smoking habits and motivation.
Free counseling for one year, according to the National Cancer Information Center.
Chat counseling is also available through a KakaoTalk channel (No Smoke Guide).

camp.title: Quit-smoking camp (regional support centers)
points: Regional smoking cessation centers run camps for heavy smokers and people who have relapsed repeatedly.
Schedules and eligibility differ by center. Check with 1544-9030 or No Smoke Guide.

tips.title: When a craving hits
items: Get comfortable and breathe deeply, or do a quick stretch.
Drink water often, and brush your teeth right after meals.
Keep candy, gum, toothpicks or ice nearby to keep your mouth and hands busy.
Change habits tied to smoking, like taking a walk instead of a coffee break.
Skip drinking for the first few weeks. Alcohol weakens your resolve.
Remember that the hard moment will pass.
tips.src: Sources: National Cancer Information Center 'Quitting in practice' (2023-06-13), MSD Manual 'Quitting smoking' (2025-04-10)

share.label: My smoke-free record
share.text: {head}, {v} saved. Calculated with the ToolHub Quit Smoking Calculator.

howTo.title: How to use
items: Enter the date and time you quit. If you leave it, the calculator shows an example of quitting 30 days ago.
Choose your tobacco type and enter how much you smoked a day (sticks for heated tobacco) and the pack price. For liquid e-cigarettes, just enter your monthly spending.
Results update every minute. Your inputs are saved on this device so you can pick up where you left off.
If you smoke again, tap 'Restart'. Your streak so far is kept as your longest record.
Save the result card as an image or share the link, and others see the same numbers.

basis.title: How it's calculated
items: Money saved = per day × (pack price ÷ cigarettes per pack) × days. For liquid e-cigarettes, the daily cost is monthly spending × 12 ÷ 365.
Not smoked = per day × days (rounded down); packs = cigarettes ÷ cigarettes per pack.
The 1-, 5- and 10-year amounts are daily cost × 365 × years, assuming today's prices stay the same.
Life regained multiplies the British study estimate of about 20 minutes per cigarette (UCL, Addiction 2024) by cigarettes not smoked. It is not a prediction of anyone's lifespan.
Recovery milestones use the WHO time points, with a month as 30 days and a year as 365 days.

items.q: How long does nicotine withdrawal last?
items.a: According to the MSD Manual, withdrawal is usually strongest in the first 2–3 days after quitting and eases within 2–4 weeks. Irritability, headaches, poor concentration, anxiety, trouble sleeping and increased appetite are common (National Cancer Information Center). If it's too hard, ask a public health center clinic or a cessation clinic about aids or medication.

items.q: Does switching to heated tobacco or a liquid e-cigarette count as quitting?
items.a: No. E-cigarettes are still a way of inhaling nicotine. The MSD Manual says evidence that they help people quit is not strong, and some devices deliver nicotine to the brain as fast as cigarettes, so the addiction risk may be similar. Korea's health insurance cessation program also treats e-cigarettes as tobacco (Gyeonggi guidance, Nov 2026), so aim to quit those too.

items.q: How should I use nicotine replacement?
items.a: Nicotine patches, gum and lozenges are usually used for 8–12 weeks. The MSD Manual says combining a long-acting patch with a fast-acting gum or lozenge more than doubles the chance of quitting long term. Doses depend on how much you smoked, so follow the product insert and your pharmacist; avoid gum if you have jaw (TMJ) problems and patches if your skin is very sensitive. Public health center clinics provide them for free.

items.q: How is the money saved calculated?
items.a: Cigarettes per day × price per cigarette (pack price ÷ cigarettes per pack) × days. At 10 a day and ₩4,500 a pack, that's ₩2,250 a day, ₩67,500 after 30 days and ₩821,250 after a year. For liquid e-cigarettes, the daily cost is monthly spending × 12 ÷ 365.

items.q: I smoked again. Do I have to start over?
items.a: Tap 'Restart' and your streak so far is kept as your longest record while the quit time resets to now. The National Cancer Information Center also encourages a new attempt after a relapse, with nicotine replacement or medication in the plan. Korea's health insurance program supports up to 3 rounds a year.

items.q: Will I gain weight after quitting?
items.a: Nicotine suppresses appetite and slightly increases calorie burning, so you may gain weight after quitting. The MSD Manual says exercise helps prevent weight gain and nicotine gum can delay it. Drink water often and keep low-calorie snacks nearby.

It's an estimate published by UCL researchers in the journal Addiction in 2024: British smokers who don't quit lose about 20 minutes of life expectancy per cigarette on average. This tool simply multiplies cigarettes not smoked by 20 minutes; it does not predict anyone's lifespan. The study covers cigarettes, so it isn't calculated for e-cigarettes.
